html:
Ever heard of the cocktail party effect?

Sound is produced by the vibration of particles in the medium, so when several people talk at once, there’s no way to make the particles split up and file into your ears in an orderly queue.

But the brain is able to choose one source, attend to it and take in its information. In a noisy setting (e.g. a cocktail party), you can still carry on a normal conversation even while the people next to you are chatting away. Or, if you’re not the least bit interested in the person talking to you and the conversation next to you is more fun, your attention gets pulled away by your neighbors, and you filter out what the person in front of you is saying, or catch only part of it. People can also pick out the sounds they’re especially sensitive to from a jumble of sources, such as their own name, or someone swearing.

Children, however, are still developing their ability to cope with noise and are not yet as good at it as adults.
